work.title: The Third Part of King Henry the Sixth

scene.label: Act 2, Scene 5
scene.title: SCENE V. Another Part of the Field

lines.text: This battle fares like to the morning's war,
lines.plainText: This battle fares like to the morning's war

lines.text: When dying clouds contend with growing light,
lines.plainText: When dying clouds contend with growing light

lines.text: What time the shepherd, blowing of his nails,
lines.plainText: What time the shepherd blowing of his nails

lines.text: Can neither call it perfect day nor night.
lines.plainText: Can neither call it perfect day nor night

lines.text: Now sways it this way, like a mighty sea
lines.plainText: Now sways it this way like a mighty sea

lines.text: Forced by the tide to combat with the wind;
lines.plainText: Forced by the tide to combat with the wind

lines.text: Now sways it that way, like the selfsame sea
lines.plainText: Now sways it that way like the selfsame sea

lines.text: Forced to retire by fury of the wind.
lines.plainText: Forced to retire by fury of the wind

lines.text: Sometime the flood prevails, and then the wind;
lines.plainText: Sometime the flood prevails and then the wind

lines.text: Now one the better, then another best,
lines.plainText: Now one the better then another best

lines.text: Both tugging to be victors, breast to breast,
lines.plainText: Both tugging to be victors breast to breast

lines.text: Yet neither conqueror nor conquered.
lines.plainText: Yet neither conqueror nor conquered

lines.text: So is the equal poise of this fell war.
lines.plainText: So is the equal poise of this fell war

lines.text: Here on this molehill will I sit me down.
lines.plainText: Here on this molehill will I sit me down

lines.text: To whom God will, there be the victory!
lines.plainText: To whom God will there be the victory

lines.text: For Margaret my queen, and Clifford too,
lines.plainText: For Margaret my queen and Clifford too

lines.text: Have chid me from the battle, swearing both
lines.plainText: Have chid me from the battle swearing both

lines.text: They prosper best of all when I am thence.
lines.plainText: They prosper best of all when I am thence

lines.text: Would I were dead, if God's good will were so;
lines.plainText: Would I were dead if God's good will were so

lines.text: For what is in this world but grief and woe?
lines.plainText: For what is in this world but grief and woe

lines.text: O God! Methinks it were a happy life
lines.plainText: O God Methinks it were a happy life

lines.text: To be no better than a homely swain;
lines.plainText: To be no better than a homely swain

lines.text: To sit upon a hill, as I do now,
lines.plainText: To sit upon a hill as I do now

lines.text: To carve out dials quaintly, point by point,
lines.plainText: To carve out dials quaintly point by point

lines.text: Thereby to see the minutes how they run:
lines.plainText: Thereby to see the minutes how they run

lines.text: How many make the hour full complete,
lines.plainText: How many make the hour full complete

lines.text: How many hours brings about the day,
lines.plainText: How many hours brings about the day

lines.text: How many days will finish up the year,
lines.plainText: How many days will finish up the year

lines.text: How many years a mortal man may live.
lines.plainText: How many years a mortal man may live

lines.text: When this is known, then to divide the times:
lines.plainText: When this is known then to divide the times

lines.text: So many hours must I tend my flock;
lines.plainText: So many hours must I tend my flock

lines.text: So many hours must I take my rest;
lines.plainText: So many hours must I take my rest

lines.text: So many hours must I contemplate;
lines.plainText: So many hours must I contemplate

lines.text: So many hours must I sport myself;
lines.plainText: So many hours must I sport myself

lines.text: So many days my ewes have been with young;
lines.plainText: So many days my ewes have been with young

lines.text: So many weeks ere the poor fools will ean;
lines.plainText: So many weeks ere the poor fools will ean

lines.text: So many years ere I shall shear the fleece.
lines.plainText: So many years ere I shall shear the fleece

lines.text: So minutes, hours, days, months, and years,
lines.plainText: So minutes hours days months and years

lines.text: Passed over to the end they were created,
lines.plainText: Passed over to the end they were created

lines.text: Would bring white hairs unto a quiet grave.
lines.plainText: Would bring white hairs unto a quiet grave

lines.text: Ah, what a life were this! How sweet, how lovely!
lines.plainText: Ah what a life were this How sweet how lovely

lines.text: Gives not the hawthorn bush a sweeter shade
lines.plainText: Gives not the hawthorn bush a sweeter shade

lines.text: To shepherds looking on their silly sheep
lines.plainText: To shepherds looking on their silly sheep

lines.text: Than doth a rich embroidered canopy
lines.plainText: Than doth a rich embroidered canopy

lines.text: To kings that fear their subjects' treachery?
lines.plainText: To kings that fear their subjects' treachery

lines.text: O, yes, it doth; a thousand-fold it doth.
lines.plainText: O yes it doth a thousandfold it doth

lines.text: And to conclude, the shepherd's homely curds,
lines.plainText: And to conclude the shepherd's homely curds

lines.text: His cold thin drink out of his leather bottle,
lines.plainText: His cold thin drink out of his leather bottle

lines.text: His wonted sleep under a fresh tree's shade,
lines.plainText: His wonted sleep under a fresh tree's shade

lines.text: All which secure and sweetly he enjoys,
lines.plainText: All which secure and sweetly he enjoys

lines.text: Is far beyond a prince's delicates—
lines.plainText: Is far beyond a prince's delicates

lines.text: His viands sparkling in a golden cup,
lines.plainText: His viands sparkling in a golden cup

lines.text: His body couched in a curious bed,
lines.plainText: His body couched in a curious bed

lines.text: When care, mistrust, and treason waits on him.
lines.plainText: When care mistrust and treason waits on him

content.text: Alarum. Enter a Son that hath killed his father, bringing in the dead body.

lines.text: Ill blows the wind that profits nobody.
lines.plainText: Ill blows the wind that profits nobody

lines.text: This man, whom hand to hand I slew in fight,
lines.plainText: This man whom hand to hand I slew in fight

lines.text: May be possessed with some store of crowns;
lines.plainText: May be possessed with some store of crowns

lines.text: And I, that haply take them from him now,
lines.plainText: And I that haply take them from him now

lines.text: May yet ere night yield both my life and them
lines.plainText: May yet ere night yield both my life and them

lines.text: To some man else, as this dead man doth me.
lines.plainText: To some man else as this dead man doth me

lines.text: Who's this? O God! It is my father's face,
lines.plainText: Who's this O God It is my father's face

lines.text: Whom in this conflict I unwares have killed.
lines.plainText: Whom in this conflict I unwares have killed

lines.text: O heavy times, begetting such events!
lines.plainText: O heavy times begetting such events

lines.text: From London by the King was I pressed forth;
lines.plainText: From London by the King was I pressed forth

lines.text: My father, being the Earl of Warwick's man,
lines.plainText: My father being the Earl of Warwick's man

lines.text: Came on the part of York, pressed by his master;
lines.plainText: Came on the part of York pressed by his master

lines.text: And I, who at his hands received my life,
lines.plainText: And I who at his hands received my life

lines.text: Have by my hands of life bereaved him.
lines.plainText: Have by my hands of life bereaved him

lines.text: Pardon me, God, I knew not what I did;
lines.plainText: Pardon me God I knew not what I did

lines.text: And pardon, father, for I knew not thee.
lines.plainText: And pardon father for I knew not thee

lines.text: My tears shall wipe away these bloody marks,
lines.plainText: My tears shall wipe away these bloody marks

lines.text: And no more words till they have flowed their fill.
lines.plainText: And no more words till they have flowed their fill

lines.text: O piteous spectacle! O bloody times!
lines.plainText: O piteous spectacle O bloody times

lines.text: Whiles lions war and battle for their dens,
lines.plainText: Whiles lions war and battle for their dens

lines.text: Poor harmless lambs abide their enmity.
lines.plainText: Poor harmless lambs abide their enmity

lines.text: Weep, wretched man, I'll aid thee tear for tear;
lines.plainText: Weep wretched man I'll aid thee tear for tear

lines.text: And let our hearts and eyes, like civil war,
lines.plainText: And let our hearts and eyes like civil war

lines.text: Be blind with tears and break o'ercharged with grief.
lines.plainText: Be blind with tears and break o'ercharged with grief

content.text: Enter a Father who has killed his son, with the body in his arms.

lines.text: Thou that so stoutly hath resisted me,
lines.plainText: Thou that so stoutly hath resisted me

lines.text: Give me thy gold, if thou hast any gold,
lines.plainText: Give me thy gold if thou hast any gold

lines.text: For I have bought it with an hundred blows.
lines.plainText: For I have bought it with an hundred blows

lines.text: But let me see: is this our foeman's face?
lines.plainText: But let me see is this our foeman's face

lines.text: Ah, no, no, no; it is mine only son!
lines.plainText: Ah no no no it is mine only son

lines.text: Ah, boy, if any life be left in thee,
lines.plainText: Ah boy if any life be left in thee

lines.text: Throw up thine eye! See, see what showers arise,
lines.plainText: Throw up thine eye See see what showers arise

lines.text: Blown with the windy tempest of my heart
lines.plainText: Blown with the windy tempest of my heart

lines.text: Upon thy wounds, that kill mine eye and heart!
lines.plainText: Upon thy wounds that kill mine eye and heart

lines.text: O, pity, God, this miserable age!
lines.plainText: O pity God this miserable age

lines.text: What stratagems, how fell, how butcherly,
lines.plainText: What stratagems how fell how butcherly

lines.text: Erroneous, mutinous, and unnatural,
lines.plainText: Erroneous mutinous and unnatural

lines.text: This deadly quarrel daily doth beget!
lines.plainText: This deadly quarrel daily doth beget

lines.text: O boy, thy father gave thee life too soon,
lines.plainText: O boy thy father gave thee life too soon

lines.text: And hath bereft thee of thy life too late!
lines.plainText: And hath bereft thee of thy life too late

lines.text: Woe above woe, grief more than common grief!
lines.plainText: Woe above woe grief more than common grief

lines.text: O that my death would stay these ruthful deeds!
lines.plainText: O that my death would stay these ruthful deeds

lines.text: O pity, pity, gentle heaven, pity!
lines.plainText: O pity pity gentle heaven pity

lines.text: The red rose and the white are on his face,
lines.plainText: The red rose and the white are on his face

lines.text: The fatal colours of our striving houses;
lines.plainText: The fatal colours of our striving houses

lines.text: The one his purple blood right well resembles,
lines.plainText: The one his purple blood right well resembles

lines.text: The other his pale cheeks, methinks, presenteth.
lines.plainText: The other his pale cheeks methinks presenteth

lines.text: Wither one rose, and let the other flourish!
lines.plainText: Wither one rose and let the other flourish

lines.text: If you contend, a thousand lives must wither.
lines.plainText: If you contend a thousand lives must wither

lines.text: How will my mother for a father's death
lines.plainText: How will my mother for a father's death

lines.text: Take on with me and ne'er be satisfied!
lines.plainText: Take on with me and ne'er be satisfied

lines.text: How will my wife for slaughter of my son
lines.plainText: How will my wife for slaughter of my son

lines.text: Shed seas of tears and ne'er be satisfied!
lines.plainText: Shed seas of tears and ne'er be satisfied

lines.text: How will the country for these woeful chances
lines.plainText: How will the country for these woeful chances

lines.text: Misthink the King and not be satisfied!
lines.plainText: Misthink the King and not be satisfied

lines.text: Was ever son so rued a father's death?
lines.plainText: Was ever son so rued a father's death

lines.text: Was ever father so bemoaned his son?
lines.plainText: Was ever father so bemoaned his son

lines.text: Was ever king so grieved for subjects' woe?
lines.plainText: Was ever king so grieved for subjects' woe

lines.text: Much is your sorrow, mine ten times so much.
lines.plainText: Much is your sorrow mine ten times so much

lines.text: I'll bear thee hence, where I may weep my fill.
lines.plainText: I'll bear thee hence where I may weep my fill

lines.text: These arms of mine shall be thy winding-sheet;
lines.plainText: These arms of mine shall be thy windingsheet

lines.text: My heart, sweet boy, shall be thy sepulchre,
lines.plainText: My heart sweet boy shall be thy sepulchre

lines.text: For from my heart thine image ne'er shall go.
lines.plainText: For from my heart thine image ne'er shall go

lines.text: My sighing breast shall be thy funeral bell;
lines.plainText: My sighing breast shall be thy funeral bell

lines.text: And so obsequious will thy father be,
lines.plainText: And so obsequious will thy father be

lines.text: Even for the loss of thee, having no more,
lines.plainText: Even for the loss of thee having no more

lines.text: As Priam was for all his valiant sons.
lines.plainText: As Priam was for all his valiant sons

lines.text: I'll bear thee hence; and let them fight that will,
lines.plainText: I'll bear thee hence and let them fight that will

lines.text: For I have murdered where I should not kill.
lines.plainText: For I have murdered where I should not kill

lines.text: Sad-hearted men, much overgone with care,
lines.plainText: Sadhearted men much overgone with care

lines.text: Here sits a king more woeful than you are.
lines.plainText: Here sits a king more woeful than you are

content.text: Alarums. Excursions. Enter Queen Margaret, Prince of Wales and Exeter.

lines.text: Fly, father, fly, for all your friends are fled,
lines.plainText: Fly father fly for all your friends are fled

lines.text: And Warwick rages like a chafed bull.
lines.plainText: And Warwick rages like a chafed bull

lines.text: Away, for death doth hold us in pursuit.
lines.plainText: Away for death doth hold us in pursuit

lines.text: Mount you, my lord; towards Berwick post amain.
lines.plainText: Mount you my lord towards Berwick post amain

lines.text: Edward and Richard, like a brace of greyhounds
lines.plainText: Edward and Richard like a brace of greyhounds

lines.text: Having the fearful flying hare in sight,
lines.plainText: Having the fearful flying hare in sight

lines.text: With fiery eyes sparkling for very wrath,
lines.plainText: With fiery eyes sparkling for very wrath

lines.text: And bloody steel grasped in their ireful hands,
lines.plainText: And bloody steel grasped in their ireful hands

lines.text: Are at our backs; and therefore hence amain.
lines.plainText: Are at our backs and therefore hence amain

lines.text: Away, for vengeance comes along with them.
lines.plainText: Away for vengeance comes along with them

lines.text: Nay, stay not to expostulate; make speed,
lines.plainText: Nay stay not to expostulate make speed

lines.text: Or else come after; I'll away before.
lines.plainText: Or else come after I'll away before

lines.text: Nay, take me with thee, good sweet Exeter;
lines.plainText: Nay take me with thee good sweet Exeter

lines.text: Not that I fear to stay, but love to go
lines.plainText: Not that I fear to stay but love to go

lines.text: Whither the Queen intends. Forward; away!
lines.plainText: Whither the Queen intends Forward away
